free_tier.stated: A test account on HLRS systems carries a contingent of 100 Hunter node hours for up to six months, granted on a one to three page application that is explicitly not peer-reviewed; GCS Preparatory Access gives a larger contingent plus HLRS user-support assistance for up to one year.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The un-peer-reviewed test account is the cheapest entry in the German stack, and it exists specifically to generate the scaling data a GCS regular or large-scale proposal needs.

limits.value: Test access is offered to potential applicants for GCS Large-Scale and rolling regular projects, which are German national calls for investigators at German research institutions, so the account presumes an eligible German home organisation.

evidence.proved: 'Within your test account you can consume a resource contingent of 100 Hunter node hours on the granted hardware platforms. The project time is limited to six months'; 'This short proposal will not be peer-reviewed', quoted

page section heading 'For investigators at German research institutions'; GCS Preparatory Access 'may last a maximum of one year' and provides 'a higher resource contingent than ordinary GCS test projects', quoted
GCS large-scale threshold 'at least 25,000 node-h on Hunter', '5,250 EFLOP on JUWELS Cluster', '140,000 GPU hours on SuperMUC-NG Phase 2', equal to 2% of each system's annual production, quoted

notes: HLRS is the only centre found that states outright that the test application is not peer-reviewed, which makes 100 Hunter node hours the most accessible German allocation; the eligibility section heading still ties it to German research institutions. Hunter carries AMD MI300A APUs, so 100 node hours is a small but real GPU allocation. GCS large-scale thresholds are useful as the corpus's clearest definition of what 'large' means in core hours versus GPU hours on the same programme.
